newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to miss EMU deficit goal -- key institutes.
newsitem.headline: Germany to miss EMU deficit goal -- key institutes.

text.p: Six economic institutes that advise the German government expected Germany to miss the deficit target for European monetary union (EMU) -- but by a narrower margin than they previously thought.

In a joint Spring report due April 22, the institutes said Germany's 1997 budget deficit would reach 3.2 percent of gross domestic product, the daily Berliner Zeitung reported in an article that will appear on Monday.

The institutes' October mid-year report predicted a ratio of 3.5 percent. Bonn has forecast a 2.9 percent gap, while the Maastricht Treaty requires a ratio of three percent for the nations that want to qualify for the EMU start in 1999.

In their new report, the research institutes concluded a shortfall in tax revenue this year would push Germany beyond the limit, the newspaper said. They expected revenues to fall 10 billion to 15 billion marks below Bonn's forecast.
Federal, state and local tax revenues in January and February were 5.5 percent below expectations, the newsweekly Focus said in an article that will appear on Monday.
The institutes also projected 2.5 percent economic growth for this year and 3.0 percent in 1998, Berliner Zeitung said.
